instruction: Take a snapshot of the video at the current position and save it as 'video_snapshot.png' on the Desktop with dimensions of at least 640x480.

parameters.window_name: Interstellar Movie - Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer - VLC media player

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires taking a screenshot with minimum dimensions. Evaluator checks if image dimensions meet the minimum requirements. Verified by reading image dimensions using PIL.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file exists at the specified location (/home/user/Desktop/video_snapshot.png)
Evaluator correctly verifies the image has minimum dimensions of 640x480 as required by the instruction
Getter logic is correct: uses env.controller.get_file() to retrieve image and PIL to extract properties (width, height, format, etc.)
Metric logic is correct: compares actual dimensions (width >= min_width and height >= min_height) against expected minimum values
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts {width, height, ...} dict -> Metric receives and checks these values
Expected values are semantically correct: min_width=640, min_height=480 matches instruction requirements exactly
Edge case handling is proper: Getter returns None if file doesn't exist or can't be read; Metric returns 0.0 if result is None
Parameter handling is correct: Metric uses expected.get('min_width') directly, not expected.get('rules', {})

Minor limitation: Cannot verify image content is actually from the video (vs. any other image), but this is practically very difficult to verify automatically and the current verification (file name + dimensions) is reasonable for this task type
